result.title: The Ephemeral Cost of Switching Optimizers Across LLM Training Stages
result.comment: Accepted to the Transitioning from Pre-Training to Post-Training Workshop at NeurIPS 2026
result.summary: Recent work suggests that switching optimizers between pretraining and subsequent training stages incurs a performance cost, but systematic investigation of this phenomenon is lacking. We study the mismatch between AdamW and Muon optimizers by pretraining 1.2B Llama-3 models from scratch while varying the proportion of updates taken with each optimizer, and similarly interpolating between the two optimizers during continued pretraining and supervised fine-tuning (SFT). Surprisingly, we find little evidence of a meaningful optimizer mismatch penalty: final performance is largely explained by the independent effects of the pretraining and post-training optimizers, with downstream performance generally improving as the proportion of Muon updates during SFT increases. Although matching the pretraining optimizer can reduce forgetting during SFT, this does not translate into improved final benchmark performance. We further evaluate AdamW and Muon for task-general SFT of open-weight models, across the Llama and Qwen families up to 14B parameters, where Muon remains competitive with AdamW, despite these models having been pretrained with AdamW. Together, our results suggest that the choice of optimizer for post-training can be made largely independently of the optimizer used during pretraining.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文系统研究 LLM 训练中预训练与后训练阶段切换优化器（AdamW 与 Muon）是否带来性能损失，通过从头预训练 1.2B Llama-3 并插值两种优化器的更新比例，发现在 SFT 等下游基准上几乎不存在有意义的优化器错配惩罚。
AI.relevance_reason: 研究的是纯文本 LLM 训练阶段的优化器选择，未涉及视觉信息保留、latent 推理状态生成与更新、证据获取或停止决策等主线问题，也未提供可迁移到 LVR 的方法线索，故排除。
